content:
According to the latest report from Bloomberg, Apple is less than two weeks away from unveiling a brand-new smart display device. The report also revealed design details of this highly anticipated smart home hub device.

Bloomberg pointed out that this home hub will feature a 6-inch square screen, with an overall design reminiscent of the classic iMac G4 — the latter adopted a hemispherical base with a metal arm supporting the screen.

According to Mark Gurman, the thickness of the device is "about the same as an iPhone," with bezels of approximately a quarter-inch in black, similar to older iPads. The corners of the body have been rounded, with "absolutely no sharp edges at all."

The following are more design details disclosed in the report:

  • The body adopts Apple's "standard gray aluminum exterior," with "rubber material added to the bottom for more stable placement."
  • The device is equipped with a USB-C port for power supply, with no built-in battery, so it must be connected to a power source at all times.
  • The bottom features a "circular metal base with multi-ring perforated speaker grille."
  • The screen is connected to the base via a "polished metal arm."
  • Users can tilt the screen forward or backward to adjust the angle.
  • The body has no volume buttons or power buttons.
  • The front features a single FaceTime camera, with no rear camera.

Bloomberg also mentioned another version of the home hub "designed for wall-mounted use." This version is also powered by USB-C, with a base that is a "slim square design positioned below the screen, with built-in speakers and microphones." According to reports, the base "will sit flush against the wall, mounted below the screen."

To read the full report, please visit Bloomberg. What are your thoughts on Apple's home hub product? Planning to get one (or even several)? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
